questions.stem: Per this page, what does `forEach` promise when the stream it ends is parallel?

options.text: Elements reach the consumer in encounter order, as on a sequential run
options.says: The page says forEach does not guarantee order in parallel streams.

options.text: Elements reach the consumer sorted by their natural ordering
options.says: Nothing on the page sorts elements for forEach; sorting takes an explicit sorted().

options.text: Elements reach the consumer in whatever sequence the threads produce
options.says: The page says forEach does not guarantee order in parallel streams, and names forEachOrdered for when order matters.

questions.stem: Why does this page prefer `Collectors.joining()` to `reduce` with `+` for concatenating many strings?

options.text: It takes elements of any type instead of needing character sequences
options.says: The page says the elements joining concatenates must be CharSequence, typically String.

options.text: It appends each piece to one builder instead of copying at every step
options.says: The page says joining uses a StringBuilder internally, while reduce with concatenation creates O(n^2) intermediate strings.

options.text: It needs no builder at all instead of filling one piece by piece
options.says: The page says joining uses a StringBuilder internally; that builder is the very reason it is efficient.
